category: Corrosion & Electrodeposition Modules: Cathodic Protection, Deforming Electrodes, Plating
description: Corrosion Module and Electrodeposition Module functionality: the Cathodic Protection interface and its anode/protected-surface nodes, boundary-element, shell and pipe current distribution interfaces, deformed-geometry corrosion and electrodeposition interfaces with their couplings, polarization-data kinetics, level-set/phase-field localized corrosion, and documented modelling workflows from the Application Libraries. Java type strings come from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Cathodic Protection (cp)
tools.description: Secondary Current Distribution interface tailored to cathodic protection, with the Enable cathodic protection features option on by default, quadratic discretization, and default tag cp. It unlocks protected, passive and thin metal surfaces, sacrificial anode surfaces, edges and points, impressed current surfaces and points, connection points and surfaces and the boundary-element Infinite Electrolyte. Used for offshore structures, ships, pipelines, monopiles and reinforced concrete.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Cathodic Protection (cp); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cp", "CathodicProtection", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electrolyte (ice1)
parameters.description: Seawater, soil or concrete conductivity (sigmal), possibly temperature dependent.

parameters.name: prop("CathodicProtection") EnableCathodicProtectionFeatures
parameters.description: On by default; the same switch exists in Secondary Current Distribution.

parameters.name: Anode and protected-surface nodes
parameters.description: Protected Metal Surface, Sacrificial Anode Surface/Edge/Point, Impressed Current Surface/Point.

tools.notes: Use a Current Distribution Initialization step of Secondary type for CP problems where ohmic drop is small. Evsref variables give protection potentials versus the adjacent reference.

tools.name: Protected Metal Surface / Thin Protected Metal Surface (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: Boundary nodes for steel surfaces assumed fully protected against metal dissolution but still active for oxygen reduction. The oxygen reduction current density is a user expression or a limited linear ramp between a zero-current potential and a limiting potential with a limiting (diffusion) current density. The node sets the electrode phase potential and defines the potential versus adjacent reference Evsref; the thin variant applies to interior boundaries (e.g. thin plates).
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Protected Metal Surface (protms1) / Thin Protected Metal Surface; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").create("protms1", "ProtectedMetalSurface", 2)

parameters.name: iO2 / iO2lim
parameters.description: Oxygen reduction current density expression or limiting current density.

parameters.name: E0, Elim
parameters.description: Zero-current potential and limiting potential of the linear ramp.

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential
parameters.description: Potential of the protected structure (e.g. from External Short or a connection DOF).

tools.notes: Coating damage can be represented by scaling the current density with a coating breakdown factor in the user expression.

tools.name: Passive Metal Surface / Thin Passive Metal Surface (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: Insulating boundary conditions for metal surfaces that pass no current (well-coated or passive), which still let you specify the electrode phase potential so that the postprocessing variable Evsref (potential versus adjacent reference) is defined. The thin variant applies to interior boundaries of electrolyte domains and defines up and down Evsref variables.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Passive Metal Surface (passms1) / Thin Passive Metal Surface (tpassms1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").create("passms1", "PassiveMetalSurface", 2)

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential
parameters.description: Used only for the Evsref postprocessing variable.

tools.notes: Exclusive exterior-boundary node on electrolyte domains.

tools.name: Sacrificial Anode Surface (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: Boundary node for dissolving sacrificial anodes on exterior electrolyte boundaries (secondary current distribution only). In time-dependent studies it solves for a remaining capacity (C/m^2) along the surface, can set all currents to zero at depletion with a smoothed step, and optionally adds tangential diffusion for convergence. Electrode Reaction subnodes define the anode dissolution kinetics, and film resistance is available.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Sacrificial Anode Surface > Electrode Reaction

parameters.name: Initial capacity
parameters.description: Charge available per area.

parameters.name: Set current density to zero at depletion / Size of transition zone
parameters.description: Depletion handling.

parameters.name: Add tangential diffusion
parameters.description: Smooths capacity gradients.

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential condition
parameters.description: As for Electrode Surface (e.g. external short to the structure).

tools.example:
1. In a Cathodic Protection model, add Sacrificial Anode Surface on the anode faces.
2. Add an Electrode Reaction with Al-Zn-In anode kinetics and Eeq = -1.05 V vs SCE.
3. Set Initial capacity from anode mass times electrochemical capacity, and run a Time Dependent study over the design life.
tools.notes: Java type string not listed in the local Application Library code; the node is described in the Corrosion Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Sacrificial Edge Anode / Wiring Edges (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: 3D edge node modelling rod-shaped sacrificial anodes as a virtual tube of shrinking radius around an edge. A capacity (C/m) is tracked in time; the radius goes from an initial radius at initial capacity to a terminal radius at depletion. The electronic potential is fixed, floating (with total current), an external short or a connection point, and the Wiring Edges subnode connects multiple separate anodes defined by the same node.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Sacrificial Edge Anode (sacredge1) > Electrode Reaction, Wiring Edges; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").create("sacredge1", "SacrificialEdgeAnode", 1)

parameters.name: Q0
parameters.description: Initial capacity per length (C/m).

parameters.name: r0, rend
parameters.description: Initial and terminal radius.

parameters.name: Electric potential model
parameters.description: Fixed, Floating, External short, Connection point or Ohm's law (with Wiring Edges).

tools.notes: Sacrificial Point Anode is the analogous point feature (spherical anode, capacity in C).

tools.name: Sacrificial Point Anode (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: Point node in 2D or 3D modelling sphere-shaped sacrificial anodes around a point, with reactions on a virtual sphere whose radius shrinks from an initial to a terminal radius as the capacity (C) is consumed in time-dependent studies. The electronic potential can be fixed, floating, an external short or a connection point.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Sacrificial Point Anode (point selection)

parameters.name: Initial radius, Terminal radius
parameters.description: Sphere radius range.

parameters.name: Initial capacity
parameters.description: Charge available per point (C).

parameters.name: Electric potential model
parameters.description: Fixed, floating, external short or connection point.

tools.example:
1. Place points at anode locations on a jacket structure.
2. Add Sacrificial Point Anode with Initial radius 0.1 m and anode Electrode Reaction.
3. Solve stationary for initial protection and time dependent for anode depletion.
tools.notes: Requires Enable Cathodic Protection Features.

tools.name: Impressed Current Surface / Impressed Current Point (ICCP)
tools.description: Active anodes of impressed current cathodic protection systems, on boundaries or points. An electrolyte potential constraint adds the current needed so that the potential difference between a sense potential and a reference potential equals the control potential, mimicking a potentiostat-controlled rectifier. The anode current can be added to the electrode phase of the protected structure to close the current loop.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Impressed Current Surface (imprcs1) / Impressed Current Point (imprcp1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").create("imprcs1", "ImpressedCurrentSurface", 2)

parameters.name: Eimpr
parameters.description: Control potential.

parameters.name: phisref_src / sense potential
parameters.description: Reference and sense potentials, typically from a Connection Point or reference electrode (e.g. root.comp1.cp.phisref_refel1).

parameters.name: Add electrode phase current contribution
parameters.description: Adds the anode current to the structure potential DOF.

tools.notes: A Reference Electrode point (type ReferenceElectrodePoint) or Connection Point supplies the reference potential.

tools.name: Connection Point / Connection Surface (Cathodic Protection)
tools.description: Nodes that implement electrical connections via wires. Connection Point (a subnode of Edge Electrode or Sacrificial Edge Anode) and Connection Surface (exterior boundary of electrode domains) define a global potential degree of freedom and enforce Kirchhoff's current law so that currents entering or leaving sum to zero. The announced potential can be used by External Short conditions, and Connection Point can define a reference electrode for impressed current control.
tools.usage: Edge Electrode > Connection Point (connp1); Cathodic Protection > Connection Surface; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").feature("edge1").create("connp1", "EdgeConnectionPoint", 0)

parameters.name: Define reference electrode
parameters.description: Adds a reference electrode potential at the point.

parameters.name: Equilibrium potential
parameters.description: Of the reference electrode.

tools.notes: Variables such as cp.phisref_connp1 are referenced by Impressed Current nodes.

tools.name: Infinite Electrolyte (Cathodic Protection, BEM)
tools.description: Boundary node representing an electrolyte of infinite extent outside the selected exterior boundaries, solved with the boundary element method (Laplace's equation) in 2D and 3D. A condition for the electrolyte potential at infinity and symmetry lines/planes (for example the sea surface) can be set. It lets a finite FEM electrolyte region near the structure be embedded in unbounded seawater.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection > Infinite Electrolyte (infice1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("cp").create("infice1", "InfiniteElectrolyte", 2)

parameters.name: sigmalInf
parameters.description: Constant electrolyte conductivity of the infinite region.

parameters.name: Infinity condition
parameters.description: Potential condition at infinity.

parameters.name: SymmetryXYPlane / SymmetryYZPlane (positions)
parameters.description: Insulating symmetry planes of infinite extent.

tools.notes: Boundaries on symmetry planes must not be included in the selection. For a pure BEM model use Current Distribution, Boundary Elements.

tools.name: Current Distribution, Boundary Elements (cdbem)
tools.description: Secondary current distribution interface solved with the boundary element method: only surfaces are meshed, and the infinite void can be included with a potential condition at infinity, which suits large or unbounded electrolytes such as seawater or soil. Symmetry planes/lines, far-field approximation with iterative solvers and quadrature settings for thin gaps are available; 3D edge features model wires and pipes as electrodes of given radius.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Primary and Secondary Current Distribution > Current Distribution, Boundary Elements (cdbem); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cdbem", "CurrentDistributionBEM", "geom1")

parameters.name: Domain selection incl. infinite void (0)
parameters.description: Include infinity in the BEM formulation.

parameters.name: prop("BEMSymmetryProp")
parameters.description: Symmetry planes, e.g. sym3 = even.

parameters.name: Use far field approximation
parameters.description: Default on with an iterative solver.

parameters.name: Edge features
parameters.description: ElectrolytePotentialEdge, ElectrolyteNormalCurrentDensityEdge with radius redge.

tools.notes: Available with Corrosion and Electrodeposition Modules. Couple to FEM regions with the Boundary Electrolyte Potential Coupling.

tools.name: Boundary Electrolyte Potential Coupling (FEM-BEM)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that passes the electrolyte phase potential computed by a finite-element current distribution interface to a boundary-element interface on shared boundaries, so that a detailed FEM region (e.g. near anodes or in soil layers) can be combined with an unbounded BEM electrolyte.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Boundary Electrolyte Potential Coupling; Source = FEM interface (cd/cp), Destination = BEM interface (cdbem)

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: FEM electrochemistry interface.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: BEM electrochemistry interface.

tools.example:
1. Model the near field of a pipeline in soil with Secondary Current Distribution (FEM).
2. Model the far field with Current Distribution, Boundary Elements.
3. Add Boundary Electrolyte Potential Coupling on the interface boundaries.
tools.notes: Java type string not listed in the local Application Library code.

tools.name: Current Distribution, Shell (cdsh)
tools.description: Interface that solves only the electrolyte potential tangentially on boundaries, representing thin electrolyte layers (films up to hundreds of micrometres) on top of electrode surfaces, as in atmospheric corrosion. The electrolyte thickness is set on the Electrolyte node, and Electrode Surface nodes share the boundary with the film. It removes meshing of thin films and anisotropy problems.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Primary and Secondary Current Distribution > Current Distribution, Shell (cdsh); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cdsh", "CurrentDistributionShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electrolyte: s, sigmal
parameters.description: Film thickness and conductivity (e.g. from relative humidity and salt load).

parameters.name: Electrode Surface (ExternalElectrodeSurface)
parameters.description: Electrode reactions under the film.

tools.notes: Available in 2D, 2D axisymmetric and 3D.

tools.name: Current Distribution, Pipe (cdpipe)
tools.description: 3D edge-based interface for electrolyte conduction inside pipes of given radius along their axis, solving only the electrolyte potential on edges. Pipe Electrode Surface defines the inner metal wall reactions, and Pipe Point Electrode Surface and Pipe Point Sacrificial Anode add point features; it greatly reduces the size of internal pipe corrosion and protection models.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Primary and Secondary Current Distribution > Current Distribution, Pipe (cdpipe); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cdpipe", "CurrentDistributionPipe", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electrolyte: redge, sigmal
parameters.description: Pipe inner radius and electrolyte conductivity.

parameters.name: Pipe Electrode Surface
parameters.description: Electrode reactions on the inner wall.

parameters.name: Pipe Point Sacrificial Anode
parameters.description: Anode coupled via a resistor with capacity tracking.

tools.notes: Only available in 3D.

tools.name: Pipe Point Sacrificial Anode (Current Distribution, Pipe)
tools.description: Point node of the pipe interface that inserts a current source representing a sacrificial anode connected to the pipe through a coupling resistance. The current depends on the local electrolyte potential, anode equilibrium potential and coupled potential; it can be restricted to anodic currents. In time-dependent studies the anode capacity is tracked with optional current cutoff at depletion.
tools.usage: Current Distribution, Pipe > Pipe Point Sacrificial Anode (ppsa1)

parameters.name: Anode equilibrium potential, Coupled potential
parameters.description: Driving potentials.

parameters.name: Coupling resistance
parameters.description: Resistor between anode and pipe.

parameters.name: Set current to zero for cathodic potentials
parameters.description: Strictly anodic current.

parameters.name: Initial capacity
parameters.description: Charge per anode (time dependent).

tools.notes: Java type in the library model: PipePointSacrificialAnode.

tools.name: Corroding Electrode (Electrode, Shell)
tools.description: Corrosion Module node of the Electrode, Shell interface that defines a shell electrode whose thickness equals a seed layer thickness plus an electrode thickness change coupled to the corrosion rate of the adjacent current distribution interface. Conductivity and an electrode current density (from the adjacent electrode reactions) complete the definition, so thinning sheets conduct less as they corrode.
tools.usage: Electrode, Shell > Corroding Electrode

parameters.name: s0
parameters.description: Seed layer (initial) thickness, default 1e-4 m.

parameters.name: Delta s
parameters.description: Electrode thickness change (e.g. from dissolution).

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Electric conductivity.

parameters.name: in
parameters.description: Electrode current density entering the shell.

tools.example:
1. Model a thin steel sheet with Electrode, Shell and add Corroding Electrode.
2. Couple Delta s to the dissolution thickness of the Electrode Surface in a Secondary Current Distribution interface.
3. Couple in to the local current density and run a time-dependent study.
tools.notes: Depositing Electrode (Electrodeposition Module) is the plating counterpart.

tools.name: Corrosion, Primary / Secondary / Tertiary (Deformed Geometry entries)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics entries that add a Primary, Secondary or Tertiary (Nernst-Planck, with electroneutrality or supporting electrolyte) current distribution interface, a Deformed Geometry interface and the Deforming Electrode Surface and Nondeforming Boundary couplings. The corroding boundaries move with the dissolution velocity computed from the electrode reactions of dissolving-depositing species, for time-dependent material-loss studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Corrosion, Deformed Geometry > Corrosion, Primary | Corrosion, Secondary | Corrosion, Tertiary with Electroneutrality (or Supporting Electrolyte)

parameters.name: Electrode Surface: Species, Ms, rhos
parameters.description: Dissolving species with molar mass and density (defines growth velocity).

parameters.name: Deforming Electrode Surface / Nondeforming Boundary
parameters.description: Coupling nodes created automatically.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent with Initialization (or Fixed Geometry variant).

tools.notes: The existing catalog entry 'Corrosion / Electrodeposition (deforming electrode interfaces)' summarises both modules; the underlying physics types are the ordinary current distribution interfaces plus Deformed Geometry.

tools.name: Deforming Electrode Surface (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Coupling that applies the deposition/dissolution velocity of Electrode Surface boundaries in an electrochemistry interface (current distribution, Lithium-Ion Battery or Battery with Binary Electrolyte) as the boundary velocity of a Deformed Geometry interface. Special tangential-velocity conditions apply at points/edges shared with nondeforming boundaries, and Moving Boundary Smoothing adds a fictitious surface tension to stabilize inherently unstable growth.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Deforming Electrode Surface (desdg1); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("desdg1", "DeformingElectrodeSurfaceDeformedGeometry", 1)

parameters.name: Echem_physics
parameters.description: Electrochemistry interface providing the velocity (cd, tcd, liion...).

parameters.name: embs
parameters.description: Moving boundary smoothing tuning parameter (0 disables).

tools.notes: Recommended manual setup: Deformed Geometry shape order 1, Hyperelastic mesh smoothing, clear the default Prescribed Mesh Displacement and add Free Deformation on deforming domains.

tools.name: Nondeforming Boundary (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Coupling for electrolyte boundaries that must not move in the normal direction (insulators, inert electrodes, symmetry boundaries) in deformed-geometry electrochemistry models. Zero normal displacement (pointwise constraints, best for planar boundaries) or zero normal velocity (for curved boundaries) can be chosen; in 3D, deformation can be restricted to a specified line.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nondeforming Boundary (ndbdg1); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ndbdg1", "NonDeformingBoundaryDeformedGeometry", 1)

parameters.name: BoundaryCondition
parameters.description: ZeroNormalDisplacement or ZeroNormalVelocity.

parameters.name: Echem_physics
parameters.description: Coupled electrochemistry interface.

parameters.name: Allow deformation along specified line only
parameters.description: 3D stabilization option.

tools.notes: Rule of thumb: zero normal displacement for planar boundaries, zero normal velocity for curved ones.

tools.name: Electrode Growth Velocity and Tangential Velocity at Corroding/Noncorroding Intersections
tools.description: Theory for moving electrode boundaries: the total growth velocity is the sum over dissolving-depositing species and electrode reactions of (stoichiometry x local current density / (n F)) x (M/rho), directed normal into the electrolyte, and the deposited thickness follows from integrated surface concentrations. At points/edges shared with noncorroding boundaries, a tangential velocity is prescribed depending on the angle between the surfaces (zero above pi), which tends to form a right angle as observed experimentally.
tools.usage: Applies to Deforming Electrode Surface with Electrode Surface dissolving-depositing species (see Deposition-Dissolution Rates, Growth Velocities and Thicknesses)

parameters.name: M_i, rho_i
parameters.description: Molar mass and density of each dissolving-depositing species.

parameters.name: nu_i, n
parameters.description: Stoichiometric coefficient and number of electrons of each reaction.

tools.example: For copper (M = 63.55 g/mol, rho = 8960 kg/m^3, n = 2) a current density of -100 A/m^2 gives a growth velocity of about 3.7e-9 m/s (13 um/h).
tools.notes: Plated or corroded thickness is often defined as a user variable from the local current density, e.g. thickness_cathode = abs(cd.iloc_er1)/2/F_const*M_Ni/rho_Ni*PlatingTime in electroplating_rack; with dissolving-depositing species the Electrode Surface also tracks surface concentrations used for thickness.

tools.name: Polarization Curve Data (interpolated local current density, Corrosion material library)
tools.description: Technique for corrosion and anodization models whose kinetics come from measured polarization curves instead of Butler-Volmer parameters. The Electrode Reaction local current density can be taken From material, using the Corrosion material library entries (LocalCurrentDensity property group with interpolation of current density versus potential vs SHE), or set to a user-defined interpolation function of the electrode potential versus reference (cd.Evsref) and temperature imported from a CSV file.
tools.usage: Electrode Reaction > Electrode Kinetics > Local current density expression = From material | User defined; Definitions > Interpolation (import CSV); Java: feature("er1").set("ilocmat_mat", "userdef"); set("ilocmat", "iloc_Al(cd.Evsref,T)")

parameters.name: ilocmat_mat
parameters.description: from_mat (material library polarization data) or userdef.

parameters.name: ilocmat
parameters.description: User expression, typically an interpolation function of Evsref (and T).

parameters.name: Interpolation function
parameters.description: source = file, filename, argument units V and degC, function unit A/m^2.

tools.notes: Make sure the reference electrode scale of the data matches the physics (Physics vs. Materials Reference Electrode Potential setting).

tools.name: Localized Corrosion with Level Set / Phase Field
tools.description: Approach for corrosion (and deposition) with large shape changes or topology changes: instead of a deformed mesh, a Level Set or Phase Field interface tracks the metal-electrolyte interface, whose normal velocity comes from the local dissolution current, while the electrochemistry is solved on a fixed mesh with the electrode reaction smeared over the interface as an Electrolyte Current Source (current density times the interface delta function). A Phase Initialization study step initializes the level-set function.
tools.usage: Secondary/Tertiary Current Distribution + Level Set (ls) with Level Set Model velocity from the corrosion rate; Electrolyte Current Source Qli = i_loc*ls.delta; Study: Phase Initialization + Time Dependent

parameters.name: Level Set Model: epsilon_ls, gamma, u
parameters.description: Interface thickness, reinitialization parameter and interface velocity.

parameters.name: Qli
parameters.description: Smeared electrode current source.

tools.notes: Handles pit coalescence or void formation that deformed-geometry models cannot continue past; requires a fine mesh around the interface.

tools.name: Galvanic Corrosion Modelling Workflow
tools.description: Documented workflow for bimetallic (galvanic) corrosion: a Secondary Current Distribution electrolyte, Electrode Surface nodes for each metal with kinetics from polarization data (Corrosion material library) sharing a common electrode potential (grounded), stationary analysis of corrosion current densities, and optionally deformed geometry to follow material loss over time. Variants study isolator thickness between dissimilar metals and zinc-coated steel.
tools.usage: Secondary Current Distribution (or Corrosion, Secondary deformed-geometry entry) + one Electrode Surface per metal; the default Electrode Surface condition (electric potential 0 V) represents the electrically connected couple

parameters.name: Electrolyte conductivity
parameters.description: E.g. brine conductivity.

parameters.name: Electrode kinetics
parameters.description: Polarization curves of each alloy (From material).

parameters.name: Dissolving species
parameters.description: Molar mass and density of the anodic metal for deformation.

tools.example: Application Library: Corrosion_Module/Galvanic_Corrosion/galvanic_corrosion_mg_alloy, galvanic_corrosion_with_deformation, isolator_thickness and galvanized_nail.
tools.notes: Mixed-potential problems usually converge better with a Secondary-type Current Distribution Initialization.

tools.name: Pitting and Crevice Corrosion Modelling
tools.description: Application approaches for localized corrosion driven by local chemistry: pitting models combine oxygen reduction mainly outside the pit, metal dissolution, species transport with electroneutrality (Tertiary Current Distribution or Aqueous Electrolyte Transport with hydrolysis equilibria) and geometry deformation; crevice models use a 1D high-aspect-ratio geometry with Aqueous Electrolyte Transport to reproduce concentration and potential differences between crevice mouth and tip.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution / Aqueous Electrolyte Transport + Electrode Surface (dissolving species) + Deformed Geometry couplings

parameters.name: Species and equilibria
parameters.description: Metal ions, hydrolysis products, chloride, H+/OH-.

parameters.name: Kinetics
parameters.description: Metal dissolution and oxygen/hydrogen reactions.

tools.example: Application Library: Corrosion_Module/Crevice_and_Pitting_Corrosion/pitting_corrosion, pitting_corrosion_stainless_steel, crevice_corrosion_fe and crevice_corrosion_with_deformation.
tools.notes: For very large shape changes see the level-set localized corrosion models.

tools.name: Atmospheric Corrosion Modelling (thin electrolyte films)
tools.description: Atmospheric corrosion occurs under thin moisture films whose thickness and conductivity depend on relative humidity and deposited salt. The documented approach uses Current Distribution, Shell for the film electrolyte on metal surfaces (e.g. aluminium alloy/steel couples, busbars), with film properties from RH and salt load, or Aqueous Electrolyte Transport for film chemistry including species equilibria and inhibitor release.
tools.usage: Current Distribution, Shell (cdsh) with Electrolyte thickness s = d_film(RH, salt load), or Aqueous Electrolyte Transport with out-of-plane thickness dz

parameters.name: Relative humidity, salt load
parameters.description: Determine film thickness and conductivity.

parameters.name: Electrode kinetics
parameters.description: Oxygen reduction limited by film diffusion and metal dissolution.

tools.example: Application Library: Corrosion_Module/Atmospheric_Corrosion/atmospheric_corrosion, atmospheric_corrosion_busbar, atmospheric_corrosion_mass_transport, evans_droplet and act_scratched_galvanized_steel; Corrosion_Module corrosion_inhibitor_transport.
tools.notes: The shell formulation avoids meshing films that are micrometres thick on large parts.

tools.name: Stray Current and AC-Induced Corrosion Modelling
tools.description: Documented approaches for interference corrosion: stray current from DC light-rail systems modelled in 3D soil with Edge Electrodes for rails and pipes, external current sources for moving trains and electrode currents at substations; AC corrosion of pipelines modelled in 1D with double-layer capacitance, first stationary with a DC bias and then transient or frequency sweeps to show the role of the double layer at higher frequencies.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection / Secondary Current Distribution with Edge Electrode, External Current Source, Electrode Current (stray current); Tertiary/Secondary with Double-Layer Capacitance and time-dependent sinusoidal potential (AC corrosion)

parameters.name: Soil conductivity zones
parameters.description: Different electrolyte domains.

parameters.name: Train current / position
parameters.description: Time- or parameter-dependent external current source.

parameters.name: AC amplitude and frequency
parameters.description: Sinusoidal potential perturbation.

tools.notes: Stray-current models use EdgeElectrode, EdgeExternalCurrentSource and EdgeElectricPotential nodes of the cp interface.

tools.name: Corrosion in Reinforced Concrete (cathodic protection, oxide jacking)
tools.description: Application approaches for rebar corrosion: cathodic protection of steel in concrete uses concrete as a moisture-dependent electrolyte, oxygen transport, iron oxidation, hydrogen evolution and oxygen reduction with a zinc anode controlled by a potentiostat; oxide jacking couples oxide-layer growth to volumetric expansion in Solid Mechanics with a scalar damage model to predict concrete cracking.
tools.usage: Cathodic Protection / Secondary Current Distribution + Transport of Diluted Species (O2) + Solid Mechanics (oxide jacking)

parameters.name: Moisture-dependent conductivity and O2 diffusivity
parameters.description: Concrete transport properties.

parameters.name: Oxide layer thickness to strain
parameters.description: Volumetric expansion driving stresses.

tools.notes: Oxide jacking requires the Structural Mechanics Module (damage model) in addition to the Corrosion Module.

tools.name: Stress Corrosion Modelling (mechano-electrochemical coupling)
tools.description: Approach for the effect of elastic and plastic deformation on corrosion rates of steel pipelines: Solid Mechanics with small-strain von Mises plasticity provides stresses and plastic strains that enter the anodic iron dissolution and cathodic hydrogen evolution kinetics (equilibrium potential shift and exchange current density change) of a current distribution model; stationary parameter studies and time-dependent corrosion follow.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics (plasticity) + Secondary Current Distribution with Electrode Reaction kinetics using stress and effective plastic strain model inputs

parameters.name: Mechanical model inputs
parameters.description: Stress tensor and effective plastic strain available as model inputs to electrode reactions.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials or Structural Mechanics Module for plasticity.

tools.name: Electrodeposition, Primary / Secondary / Tertiary (Deformed Geometry entries)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics entries of the Electrodeposition Module adding a primary, secondary or tertiary (electroneutrality or supporting electrolyte) current distribution interface, a Deformed Geometry interface and Deforming Electrode Surface/Nondeforming Boundary couplings. The cathode moves with the deposition velocity, giving plated thickness distributions, feature filling and shape evolution over time.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Electrodeposition, Deformed Geometry > Electrodeposition, Primary | Secondary | Tertiary with Electroneutrality | Tertiary with Supporting Electrolyte

parameters.name: Depositing species
parameters.description: Metal molar mass and density on the Electrode Surface.

parameters.name: Electrode reactions
parameters.description: Metal deposition and side reactions (e.g. hydrogen evolution).

parameters.name: Couplings
parameters.description: Deforming Electrode Surface / Nondeforming Boundary.

tools.notes: Use Automatic Remeshing in the time-dependent solver for large deformations; switch to level set when voids form.

tools.name: Depositing Electrode (Electrode, Shell)
tools.description: Electrodeposition Module node of the Electrode, Shell interface for thin seed layers whose thickness grows by deposition: thickness = seed layer thickness + electrode thickness change coupled from the deposition rate, with electric conductivity and electrode current density from the adjacent current distribution interface. It captures the terminal effect on resistive wafers, where lateral seed-layer resistance makes plating nonuniform.
tools.usage: Electrode, Shell > Depositing Electrode (depe1); Java type: "DepositingElectrode"

parameters.name: s0
parameters.description: Seed layer thickness (default 1e-4 m).

parameters.name: Delta s
parameters.description: Electrode thickness change from deposition.

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Electric conductivity.

parameters.name: in
parameters.description: Electrode current density from the electrolyte side.

tools.example: Application Library: Electrodeposition_Module/Tutorials/resistive_wafer (terminal effect on a patterned wafer).
tools.notes: Solve with a Secondary-type Current Distribution Initialization followed by Time Dependent.

tools.name: Trench and Via Filling with Level Set / Phase Field (Electrodeposition)
tools.description: Approach for copper filling of trenches and vias where the deposit front may pinch off and form voids: the Tertiary Current Distribution (Cu2+/SO4 2- with electroneutrality) is solved on a fixed mesh, and a Level Set or Phase Field interface moves the metal/electrolyte interface with the local deposition velocity, handling the topology change that stops deformed-geometry models. Additive (suppressor) effects can be included via surface coverage.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution + Level Set (ls) or Phase Field (pf) + Highly Conductive Porous Electrode/Electrolyte Current Source representation of the deposit; Phase Initialization + Time Dependent study

parameters.name: Interface velocity
parameters.description: From deposition current density, molar mass and density of copper.

parameters.name: Interface thickness
parameters.description: Level set epsilon_ls or phase field thickness.

tools.example: Application Library: Electrodeposition_Module/Tutorials_with_Deforming_Geometries/cu_trench_deposition (deformed geometry), cu_trench_deposition_ls and cu_trench_deposition_pf.
tools.notes: The level-set version continues to 20 s, beyond cavity formation, whereas the deformed-geometry model must stop at pinch-off.

tools.name: Pulse Reverse Plating Modelling
tools.description: Tutorial approach for additive-free leveling of protrusions by pulse reverse plating: a secondary current distribution with Butler-Volmer kinetics is solved for forward and reverse pulses, assuming a quasi-stationary current distribution in each pulse, and the averaged deposition rate over the duty cycle drives a deformed-geometry simulation. Electrolyte Current conditions set the forward and reverse current densities.
tools.usage: Secondary Current Distribution with Electrolyte Current (forward/reverse) + Deformed Geometry with Prescribed Normal Mesh Velocity from the averaged rate

parameters.name: Forward/reverse current densities and pulse lengths
parameters.description: Duty cycle parameters.

parameters.name: Averaged deposition velocity
parameters.description: Combines the two stationary solutions.

tools.notes: The library model uses PrescribedNormalMeshVelocityDeformedGeometry and PrescribedNormalMeshDisplacementDeformedGeometry nodes.

tools.name: Rotating Cylinder Hull Cell (primary vs secondary vs tertiary)
tools.description: Verification example simulating current, potential and concentration distributions along the working electrode of a rotating cylinder Hull cell in 2D axisymmetry, comparing primary, secondary and tertiary current distributions to show how kinetics and mass transport progressively change plating uniformity. It demonstrates stepwise model building from Primary Current Distribution to Tertiary.
tools.usage: Primary Current Distribution -> Secondary Current Distribution -> Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck in a 2D axisymmetric model with Electrolyte Potential and Electrode Surface boundaries

parameters.name: Current distribution type
parameters.description: Primary, secondary, tertiary.

parameters.name: Rotation-dependent mass transfer
parameters.description: Diffusion layer thickness for tertiary case.

tools.notes: A good template for comparing Wagner numbers and throwing power of plating baths.

tools.name: Alloy and Electroless Deposition Modelling
tools.description: Tutorial approaches beyond single-metal plating: Ni-P alloy codeposition solved in a 1D diffusion layer with the Tertiary Current Distribution for six species and competing Ni, P and hydrogen evolution reactions, giving polarization and deposit composition; and copper electroless deposition, where copper reduction and formaldehyde oxidation occur at the same surface at a mixed potential determined by zero net current, with concentration-dependent equilibrium potentials.
tools.usage: Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck with multiple Electrode Reaction nodes on one Electrode Surface; for electroless, Electrode Surface with Total current = 0

parameters.name: Multiple Electrode Reactions
parameters.description: Partial reactions sharing one electrode potential.

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: Electrode potential sweep (alloy) or total current zero (mixed potential).

tools.notes: Deposit composition follows from the ratio of partial deposition currents.

tools.name: Electrochemical Machining (ECM) Modelling
tools.description: Tutorial for anodic dissolution shaping: a primary current distribution between a cathode tool and an anode workpiece (20 V applied) in 2D axisymmetry, with high-velocity electrolyte feed, drives deformed-geometry evolution of a microbore; insulating layers shape the dissolution. Electrode domains are replaced by boundary potentials because of high metal conductivity.
tools.usage: Primary Current Distribution + Deformed Geometry couplings (Electrodeposition, Primary entry), Axial Symmetry

parameters.name: Applied voltage
parameters.description: Potential difference tool/workpiece.

parameters.name: Dissolving metal properties
parameters.description: Molar mass and density for removal rate.

tools.notes: Gas evolution at the cathode is neglected in the tutorial.

tools.name: Plating Uniformity Optimization (shields, racks, shape optimization)
tools.description: Approaches for improving deposit thickness uniformity: secondary current distribution with Butler-Volmer kinetics for multiple parts on a rack, insulating shields modelled as Thin Electrolyte Layers, and Shape Optimization studies that move shield aperture boundaries (free shape domain) to minimize a p-norm of thickness deviation on a printed circuit board.
tools.usage: Secondary Current Distribution + Thin Electrolyte Layer (Insulating) + Study > Shape Optimization (sho) with Free Shape Domain/Boundary and a P-Norm objective

parameters.name: Objective
parameters.description: Deviation of deposited thickness from mean (p-norm).

parameters.name: Design variables
parameters.description: Aperture shape via free shape boundary.

tools.example:
Application Library: Electrodeposition_Module/Tutorials/pcb_aperture_optimization, electroplating_rack and decorative_plating.
model.study("std1").create("sho", "ShapeOptimization");
tools.notes: Shape optimization requires the Optimization Module.

tools.name: Time-Dependent with Initialization, Fixed Geometry (study)
tools.description: Study available with the Electrodeposition and Corrosion Modules that adds a Current Distribution Initialization step followed by a Time Dependent, Fixed Geometry step, which excludes the deformed-geometry (ALE X, Y, Z) variables from the solution. It is used when mesh deformation is expected to be small, or to compute deposit thickness without moving the mesh.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Multiphysics > Time Dependent with Initialization, Fixed Geometry

parameters.name: Current Distribution Initialization type
parameters.description: Primary or secondary.

parameters.name: Times
parameters.description: Output times of the fixed-geometry time-dependent step.

tools.example:
1. Build an Electrodeposition, Secondary model.
2. Add Time Dependent with Initialization, Fixed Geometry and set Times = range(0,60,3600).
3. Plot the deposited thickness variable on the cathode without deforming the mesh.
tools.notes: Java type strings for this preset study are not given in the local documentation.
